item.title: backlog history and status read full JSONL archive to show last N items
item.intent: Both 'backlog history' and 'status' commands read the entire sprints.jsonl archive through jq before applying tail, causing O(n) work when only O(k) is needed. Archive reads must be bounded by the display limit, not file size.
item.description: Two commands process the entire sprints.jsonl archive unnecessarily before taking the last few records. In 'backlog history' (default --limit 20), jq processes all N records then 'tail -n 20' discards all but the last 20. In '_status_output', jq processes all N records then 'tail -5' keeps only 5. Since sprints.jsonl is JSONL (one JSON object per line), 'tail -n N file | jq ...' gives the same result with O(k) file I/O instead of O(n). The archive grows by one line per sprint, so this gets progressively worse.
steps: In cmd_backlog_history (lines ~4797-4802): replace 'jq -r ... "$sprints_file" | tail -n "$limit"' with 'tail -n "$limit" "$sprints_file" | jq -r ...'
Verify both changes produce the same output as before when archive has <limit items
Verify output is correct when archive has exactly limit items and more than limit items
Run shellcheck and confirm zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: backlog history output is identical to before when total records <= limit
backlog history shows last N records in reverse-chronological order when total > limit
status recent sprints shows last 5 records correctly
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
